title: 2027-08-19 Novelle Health renewal + EU private onboarding planning
next_steps: Redwood to send updated term sheet + regional pricing by 2027-08-23
SE to run EU on-prem perf benchmark with Novelle test rig week of 8/30
Customer to provide final list of compliance docs needed by 8/25
action_items: Alex Morales - Draft and share amendment language for 12-month renewal and EU on-prem pilot - 2027-08-23
Priya Nair - Schedule and run perf bench (Llama-XL analog workload) on customer's on-prem node and share results - week of 2027-08-30
Lena Fischer - Share network/VPN/peering details + firewall egress window with Redwood - 2027-08-25
Peter Gold - Confirm procurement timeline and PO cadence for committed capacity uplift - 2027-09-01
summary: Renewal check-in focused on contract extension, capacity uplift, and planning a EU private (on-prem/VPC) pilot. Customer wants predictable latency and data residency; raised SOC 2/ISO needs, KMS integration, and an explicit fallback plan to hosted during pilot. Redwood AE outlined pricing amendment and next steps for benchmarks and security docs.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-08-19 15:00 UTC | Duration: 48 minutes | Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (SE), Ethan (TAM) / Maya (Head of ML), Jonas (CTO), Lena (Cloud Ops), Peter (Procurement)

[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you all making time. Quick agenda — renewal terms, capacity uplift for Q4, and the EU private onboard pilot. We'll run through the pricing amendment and Priya will talk perf/bench plan.
[00:20] Maya: Thanks Alex, yeah we wanted this to be fairly focused. We're near end of term and want to lock in 12 months but also add dedicated capacity in eu-west and an on-prem pilot in our Frankfurt colo for data residency.
[00:35] Jonas: Right, performance is biggest ask; we saw token latency spikes during our internal load tests. Also need clarity on encryption and KMS integration, we can't have unencrypted kv caches.
[00:50] Priya: Understood, quick clarifier — when you say on-prem pilot, do you mean full private control plane or a customer-managed runtime with Redwood operators?
[01:05] Lena: We want customer-managed runtime, basically VPC-like but in our colo. We need the ability to rotate keys via our HSM and no model or prompt data leaving the rack.
[01:20] Ethan: Ok that's doable, Redwood Private supports a customer-managed control plane and HSM/KMS integrations. For the initial pilot we typically do a hybrid: private runtime in your colo, control plane in a regulated region, with strict egress rules. We'll document the exact network requirements.
[01:45] Peter: From procurement — timeline is tight. If we agree terms this week we'd target PO by end of month. We need an amendment rather than a full new SOW to speed it up.
[02:05] Alex: Makes sense, we can prepare an amendment for a 12-month renewal that includes an initial committed uplift of X RU (redwood units) and an on-prem pilot line item. I'll send that by Tuesday.
[02:20] Maya: Also want to discuss fallback — if the pilot has any perf regressions, can we fall back to hosted in eu-west while we debug?
[02:35] Priya: Yes, we support automated routing fallback. Practically, we recommend a canary window and automatic failover policy so traffic goes to hosted instance with pinned model version. There is a small cost delta but it keeps production availability up.
[02:55] Jonas: How about KV cache behavior — we saw cache warmup causing token latency at peak. Any tuning knobs?
[03:10] Priya: There are batching and prefix-KV caching strategies; for your workload we think continuous batching with pre-warmed KV for the most common conversation flows will reduce tail latency. We'll include suggested profiles in the bench run.
[03:35] Lena: Network: we need exact port list and CIDR ranges for our security team. Also, do you require a peering or can we use a VPN?
[03:50] Ethan: We can support both. For lower latency peering is recommended but VPN is supported for pilot. We'll provide firewall rules and a sample peering template.
[04:05] Maya: Compliance: SOC 2 type II evidence, ISO attestation, and audit logs retention policy. Our legal team will want to see retention window for logs and access logs for model queries.
[04:25] Alex: We'll share SOC 2 package and the audit log spec. For logs retention we can offer configurable retention; default is 90 days but enterprise add-on supports 365 days.
[04:40] Jonas: KMS — we are 100% with AWS KMS + AWS CloudHSM fallback. We want Redwood to call our KMS for envelope keys and not store plaintext anywhere.
[04:55] Priya: That's the standard. For private/on-prem we can configure the runtime to call your KMS/HSM. We'll document the handshake — typically we use envelope encryption and never persist plaintext on disk.
[05:10] Maya: Can you confirm if there are any limitations on model variants for private infra? We prefer quantized LLMs for cost, but want the same API semantics as hosted.
[05:25] Priya: The runtime supports the same API; model variants are available but some quantization paths require specific kernel support. For your colo hardware profile we'll recommend model/quant combos that match latency targets.
[05:45] Alex: On pricing — we proposed a 15% discount for a 12-month renewal plus committed capacity. The EU private pilot is a one-time setup fee and a small monthly management add-on. I'll include a few options (12m, 24m) in the amendment.
[06:05] Peter: For procurement we need line items separated: committed tokens RU, pilot setup, managed support, and optional audit retention add-on.
[06:20] Alex: Noted, will do.
[06:30] Maya: Benchmarks — can Redwood run a load test against a mirror of our traffic patterns? We want p50/p95/p99 across short and long contexts.
[06:45] Priya: Yes, we'll run the Llama-XL analogue benchmark with your example prompts if you provide a sanitized dataset. For the on-prem run we'll need access to the test node and some scheduling — estimate 3 days to run and analyze.
[07:05] Jonas: Is there a documented SLA for latency and throughput for Dedicated vs Private?
[07:20] Ethan: Yes, Dedicated gets SLA-backed throughput and latency targets; Private SLA can be contracted — for pilot we usually treat it as best-effort until the node is fully validated. We'll propose an SLA uplift as part of the amendment if you want a formal guarantee.
[07:45] Lena: Our security team also asked about RBAC and SSO — we use SAML 2.0 and want group-based roles to map to environments.
[07:55] Priya: Redwood supports SAML SSO and RBAC mapping to roles. For Private we can integrate with your IdP during provisioning.
[08:10] Maya: Great. One more question — if we increase capacity mid-term, is pricing pro-rated?
[08:25] Alex: Typically yes, uplifts are pro-rated for the remainder of the term. We'll include a simple uplift table in the amendment.
[08:40] Peter: If we sign this week, can you reserve the EU capacitated nodes for our pilot in September?
[08:55] Ethan: We can tentatively reserve but need signature on amendment to hold dedicated capacity; otherwise capacity is best-effort. We'll mark it as 'hold' for 7 days pending the PO.
[09:10] Maya: Ok — let's recap next steps.
[09:20] Alex: Recap: 1) Redwood will send amendment + pricing options by 2027-08-23; 2) Priya to schedule bench run week of 2027-08-30 (on-prem node) and prepare suggested runtime profiles; 3) Redwood to send SOC 2 and audit log spec by 8/23; 4) Novelle to share sanitized prompt set and network peering/VPN details by 8/25; 5) Procurement aims to issue PO by 2027-09-01.
[09:50] Maya: That sounds right. Does anyone have blockers?
[10:00] Jonas: Minor — we'd like a short runbook for fallback to hosted in case of regression.
[10:10] Priya: We'll include a rollback runbook and traffic routing policy in the bench readout.
[10:25] Peter: From legal side, we may want to confirm IP language but that's downstream — procurement will flag it.
[10:35] Alex: Great. We'll follow up on the action items. Thanks everyone.

Transcript notes: occasional overlapping talk, some transcription noise (e.g., 'kv' transcribed as 'kev' in places in auto-captions), proper nouns sometimes garbled.

End of meeting.
